question: Shared: do older adults with MCI differ from healthy controls in walking performance under a simple condition and under a more demanding one? Both papers use the gait/motor channel. P-687 measures stopwatch Timed Up and Go (TUG) time, single-task and with a phone-dialling dual task, in 30 MCI v 30 HC in Guangzhou. P-1082 measures Kinect gait markers during single-task straight and curved (oval) walking in 25 MCI v 30 HC in Iran. The instrument and the kind of added demand differ, which condition 1 allows.
metric: Direction of the MCI-HC group difference in both: TUG completion time in P-687, walking velocity and other markers in P-1082.

figures.P-1082: Straight walk velocity: HC 50.13 +/- 27.92 v MCI 47.39 +/- 9.80 cm/s, p = 0.780. Difference 2.74 cm/s slower in MCI, SE = sqrt(27.92^2/30 + 9.80^2/25) = 5.46, CI [-7.96, 13.44]; d = 0.13 (CI -0.40 to 0.66). Curve walk velocity: 45.90 +/- 8.89 v 39.27 +/- 10.09 cm/s, p = 0.007. Difference 6.63 cm/s, CI [1.55, 11.71]; d = 0.70 (CI 0.15 to 1.25). In-sample ROC AUC 0.83 (curve) v 0.78 (straight).

matched_figure_check: The matched figures exist and reconcile the pair. Under the simple condition (single-task TUG; straight walk), both papers find no MCI-HC difference, with overlapping effect-size intervals (-0.62 to 0.39 against -0.40 to 0.66). Under the demanding condition (dual-task TUG; curved walk), both find MCI worse, with nearly identical standardised effects (d 0.67 against 0.70).
performance_validity: Not a performance comparison between the two papers. P-687 reports no discrimination metric, and P-1082's in-sample AUCs (0.78, 0.83) are below 0.97 and are not set against anything in P-687.
reason: The two papers agree. Each finds no MCI-HC difference in the simpler walking condition and a significant, similar-sized deficit (d about 0.7) in the more demanding one, so no difference beyond uncertainty exists and the matched figures reconcile them (conditions 3 and 4). The record itself places both papers on the same side and argues against other studies (P-761, P-695) that are not part of this pair.

quotes.quote: There was no significant difference in the single task execution time between the MCI and HC groups (MCI: 17.29 ± 2.34 s, HC: 17.60 ± 2.89 s, t = 0.47, p = 0.643).
However, a significant difference in the execution time of the dual-task paradigm was observed between the two groups (MCI: 29.23 ± 8.02 s, HC: 24.92 ± 4.42 s, t = −2.58, p = 0.012).
We employed a Kinect v.2 camera to record the gait of 55 older adults (30 healthy controls, 25 with MCI) during single-task straight and curve walking tests.
the area under the curve (AUC) for curved path walking (0.83) was significantly higher than for straight path walking (0.78)
